config.title: Toggle Visibility

intro.title: Toggle Visibility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive component that can show or hide content when a user clicks a button. You'll learn how to use Angular's property binding and event handling to control element visibility dynamically. The core programming concept involves managing component state with boolean variables and using Angular's built-in directives like *ngIf or [hidden] to conditionally display elements. You'll work with TypeScript methods, click event handlers, and Angular's template syntax to create a responsive user interface. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how to implement toggle functionality that's commonly used in dropdown menus, collapsible sections, and modal dialogs.
intro.usecase: Toggle visibility is one of the most common patterns in modern web applications, appearing in navigation menus that collapse on mobile devices, accordion sections in FAQ pages, and expandable sidebar panels in admin dashboards. You'll find this pattern in form wizards where sections show/hide based on user selections, shopping cart dropdowns that appear on hover, and notification panels that slide in from the side. Developers use toggle visibility to create cleaner interfaces by hiding secondary content until needed, such as advanced filter options in e-commerce sites or detailed project information in task management tools like Trello or Asana.

objectives: Initialize a boolean property to control element visibility state
Implement a click handler method to toggle visibility values
Apply Angular's structural directive to conditionally render elements
Bind click events to toggle buttons in component templates
Configure dynamic CSS classes based on visibility state
Manipulate DOM element display through property interpolation
Construct interactive UI components with show/hide functionality

steps.title: Import Component from Angular core
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the Component decorator from the Angular core package
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a utility from a library
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Component decorator is imported and available for use in creating Angular components
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with the import statement. Make sure you're importing Component from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: use the import statement to bring in the Component decorator from the @angular/core package.

steps.title: Create the ToggleVisibility component class
steps.instruction: Create a component class named ToggleVisibility and decorate it with @Component. Add basic metadata including selector 'app-toggle-visibility' and an empty template.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator above the class declaration. The decorator takes an object with selector and template properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ToggleVisibility component class decorated with @Component, including selector and template metadata
successCriteria: ToggleVisibility class is created with @Component decorator, selector 'app-toggle-visibility', and template property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your component class is named ToggleVisibility and includes both selector and template in the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a class named ToggleVisibility and decorate it with @Component. The decorator should include selector and template properties.

steps.title: Initialize the visibility state property
steps.instruction: Add a boolean property named 'isVisible' to the ToggleVisibility class and initialize it to true
steps.hint: In Angular components, properties are declared directly in the class body. Use TypeScript syntax: propertyName: type = initialValue;
steps.expectedOutcome: The ToggleVisibility component will have an isVisible property initialized to true, which will be used to track whether content should be shown or hidden
successCriteria: The ToggleVisibilityComponent class contains an isVisible property of type boolean initialized to true
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the property is named 'isVisible', is of type boolean, and is initialized to true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isVisible property should be declared inside the component class with the syntax: isVisible: boolean = true;

steps.title: Define the toggle method
steps.instruction: Create a method named 'toggleVisibility' inside the ToggleVisibilityComponent class that toggles the isVisible property between true and false.
steps.hint: Use 'this.isVisible = !this.isVisible' to toggle the boolean value. Methods in Angular components are defined as regular class methods.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class will have a toggleVisibility method that switches the isVisible property between true and false when called.
successCriteria: A method named 'toggleVisibility' is defined that uses 'this.isVisible = !this.isVisible' to toggle the boolean state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your method is named 'toggleVisibility' and uses '!this.isVisible' to toggle the boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a method named 'toggleVisibility' that assigns 'this.isVisible = !this.isVisible' to toggle the boolean state.

steps.title: Add the basic template structure
steps.instruction: Replace the empty template string with a div element that has the class 'container'
steps.hint: Add a div with a class attribute inside the template property. The div will serve as the main container for your toggle visibility content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will contain a div element with the class 'container' that will serve as the main wrapper for the toggle visibility functionality.
successCriteria: Template contains a div element with class attribute set to 'container'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your div element has the class attribute set to 'container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain a div element with class='container'. Check that you're replacing the empty template string with the proper HTML structure.

steps.title: Add the toggle button with click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the div container with the text 'Toggle Visibility' and bind its click event to the toggleVisibility method using Angular's event binding syntax.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click) to bind the button's click event to your toggleVisibility method. The button should be placed inside the div container.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button with click event binding
<button (click)="saveData()">Save</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button with 'Toggle Visibility' text that is bound to the toggleVisibility method using Angular's click event binding.
successCriteria: Button element is added inside the div with text 'Toggle Visibility' and (click) event binding to toggleVisibility method
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your button has the correct text 'Toggle Visibility' and uses Angular's (click) event binding syntax to call the toggleVisibility method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button needs to be added inside the div container with the text 'Toggle Visibility' and should use Angular's event binding syntax (click) to call the toggleVisibility method.

steps.title: Add the content to be toggled
steps.instruction: Inside the div, add a paragraph element with the text 'This content can be toggled!'
steps.hint:
Add a

tag with sample text that will be shown or hidden based on the toggle state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: adding content to display

Welcome to our app!
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element is added to the template with sample text that will be toggled.
successCriteria: The template contains a paragraph element with the text 'This content can be toggled!'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're adding a paragraph element with the specified text inside the div.
steps.feedbackWrong:
Not quite right. Add a

element with the text 'This content can be toggled!' inside the div in your template.

steps.title: Apply conditional visibility with ngIf
steps.instruction: Add the *ngIf directive to the paragraph element to control its visibility based on the isVisible property
steps.hint: Use the *ngIf structural directive with the isVisible property to conditionally show or hide the paragraph
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: conditional rendering with *ngIf

This message appears conditionally
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph element will have the *ngIf directive that references the isVisible property, making it conditionally visible
successCriteria: The paragraph element includes the *ngIf="isVisible" directive
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the *ngIf directive references the isVisible property correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: add the *ngIf structural directive to the paragraph element and reference the isVisible property.

steps.title: Update button text based on visibility state
steps.instruction: Use string interpolation to make the button text dynamic - show 'Hide Content' when content is visible, and 'Show Content' when content is hidden.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator inside double curly braces to conditionally display different text based on the isVisible property value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: dynamic text based on state
<button>{{ isLoggedIn ? 'Logout' : 'Login' }}</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button text will dynamically change between 'Hide Content' and 'Show Content' based on the current visibility state.
successCriteria: Button text uses string interpolation with a ternary operator to show 'Hide Content' when isVisible is true and 'Show Content' when isVisible is false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using string interpolation {{ }} with a ternary operator to show different text based on the isVisible property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button text should change dynamically. Use {{ isVisible ? 'Hide Content' : 'Show Content' }} inside the button element to show different text based on the current state.

steps.title: Test the toggle functionality
steps.instruction: Click the toggle button to verify that the content shows and hides correctly when the button is pressed.
steps.hint: Look for the 'Toggle Content' button in the preview and click it multiple times to see the paragraph appear and disappear.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: testing a light switch
// Click the switch to turn lights on/off
steps.expectedOutcome: The toggle functionality works correctly - clicking the button alternates between showing and hiding the paragraph content.
successCriteria: The button successfully toggles the visibility of the paragraph when clicked, demonstrating the complete toggle functionality.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good progress! The component structure is correct. Make sure to test the button functionality in the preview to see the toggle behavior.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle functionality isn't working as expected. Check that the button's (click) handler calls toggleVisibility() and that the paragraph uses *ngIf="isVisible" to control visibility.
